tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate 18%). Actions taken: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was only in staging and is also unhealthy). The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the service mixed (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1). I re-ran the rollback to v2.3.0, which completed in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: healthy, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure and the orchestrator partial-failure before re-deploying v2.3.1.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it is healthy again (error rate 0.2%, down from 18%). I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 is unhealthy, and v2.3.1-rc was only deployed to staging. Because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production, no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Partial failure:** The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the service mixed. I re-ran the same rollback, and it completed in us-east, us-west and eu-west.
- **Incident timeout:** The first incident request timed out. I retried with the same idempotency key, and the service returned a single incident, so there should be no duplicate.

The incident summary covers the rollback, the partial failure, and the follow-up work. That work is to investigate the v2.3.1 failure and the orchestrator error before anyone re-deploys v2.3.1.
